title: Review: Mixed feeings on this one.  A lot of individually great momen...
transcript: Do not be fooled by its title, Chinese Republicans is not about politics. It's really a play about career ambition and the lengths that people will go to to propel themselves forwards, even if it's at the expense of others. And it's told through the lens of four Chinese Americans, each with varying perspectives. And one of the core themes of the show is exploring the ways in which these women, who yes, are Republican, are betraying their own communities in order to be accepted by their predominantly white and male co-workers. But this play also explores many other themes, including the cost of assimilation, cultural clashes within the Chinese community, generational differences, the difficulties of being a woman in the workplace. And because of that, this play does feel a little bit over stuffed given that it's only a 90 minute run time. And I wish that the playwright had either scaled back the number of topics that they wanted to cover or just written a longer play, because while individual parts of this play are very good, it never quite comes together in the way that I think the playwright wanted it to. I do still think this play is worth seeing, if not only because the Chinese American perspective is not one that we get in American theatre all that often. And I do hope the playwright continues to develop this piece because it does have a lot of potential. It just needs a little bit More time in the oven
reasoning: Creator finds individual parts good and says it's worth seeing, but criticizes it as overstuffed and not cohering, needing more development. Lands squarely in mixed territory with a mild lean positive.
